## The question

[Creating a complex template](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/11937/creating-a-complex-template), asked by [ipavlic](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/1688/ipavlic) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-02-24; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> I would like to create a complex template for documentation as a document class. 
>
> I should be able to define my `text` fields (for instance, `\documentNumber`, `\projectTitle`). My class should be flexible enough to accomodate landscape pages as well. `XeTeX` is preferrable.
>
> This is a sketch of how the document template should look like:
>
> ![Layout sketch][q-1]
>
> The only idea I had was to [create a tikzpicture on every page,  as described in my other question][q-2]. I got recommendations for using `everypage`, `everyshi` and such. I was hoping for more specific answers. Code snippets or just outlined concepts for coding are most welcome.
>
> [q-1]: AWjAt.png
>   [q-2]: https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/4930/tikzpicture-on-every-page
:::

You might try the [`textpos`](http://ctan.org/pkg/textpos) package or some of the other solutions described on the TeX FAQ page ["Putting things at fixed positions on the page"](https://texfaq.org/FAQ-abspos).

If you are comfortable using TikZ to do this kind of thing don't be afraid to.  Yes, it's a lot of "overhead" but it works.

Although I know very little about it I hear ConTeXt does this kind of thing well.  So we should be getting an answer from one of their users soon.
